newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended sharply higher on Tuesday, after a volatile and busy day.
The 6.25 percent July 1998 bond ended unchanged at 104.18/26, yielding 3.32 percent at bid, while the 30-year bond was up 46 basis points at 112.96/113.16, yielding 6.45 pct.
Trade was heavy in the Jan 2006 and the 30-year bonds.

Initial losses were recouped as the release of U.S. December CPI data relieved the market. The overall CPI showed an expected 0.3 percent increase, but the core figure excluding food and energy prices rose only 0.1 percent, below expectations.
U.S. December retail sales, which were up more than expected (+0.6 percent), could not temper enthusiasm on the U.S. market.
"The CPI apparently weighed most, boosting U.S. Treasuries. Europe just follows them, although we might be creating an air bubble," one dealer said.
Dealers said sentiment on the Dutch bond market remained positive in spite of the high price levels, causing a flattening of the yield curve.
"Players are lengthening their positions. They buy the 30-year bond, or just switch from the 1999s to bonds maturing in 2000," one dealer said.
With more important economic data ahead this week, dealers said the market was likely to remain volatile for a while.
On Friday, the Dutch state is to announce a tap issue, which also claimed attention. Players are divided on its maturity, but most expect a reopening of the September 2002 bond.

"The state will issue a short term bond. Anxiety over the state's preference for loans with a shorter maturity has driven prices of the ten-year bonds higher. I don't think there are many shorts left in the February 2007 8.25 pct, so if the state does decide to add a tranche to that one, demand is set to deflate," one dealer said.
